text:
tess: paging: SLOs climbing, error-rate spike to 4.8% across hosted clusters, saw KV cache eviction+miss storm after YaRN sliding-window prefetch was enabled in canary this morning. tagging @adrian @maya @kai :rotating_light:
incident-bot: page triggered for service=runtime kv_cache_evictions rate>threshold (hosted-us-east-1)
eli: seeing multiple customer reports about timeouts for long-context requests (>=20k tokens). customers hitting 429/503s on generation endpoints.
adrian: on it. which canary? I saw a canary deploy around 1945600000 that toggled continuous.prefetch=true for longctx models (NTK/YaRN combo).
tess: canary id: canary-2026-05-17-12:40, commit: 8f3c2b4. confirmed metric jump at ~1945665000.
maya: kv_cache_size and kv_cache_evictions both spiked, Redis-ish eviction not same pattern — this looks like internal rope/KV in-memory blowout (continuous batching + sliding window prefetch interacting).
kai: NTK prefetch was changed to sliding-window with lookahead=1024 in that canary. That will pre-populate KV entries aggressively. probably touching many key prefixes and blowing the eviction policy.
adrian: ok mitigation plan: 1) flip continuous.prefetch=false in canary/hosted config via runtime-config API 2) scale down longctx pool (reduce concurrency) 3) reduce batching.window_ms to 20ms for affected models 4) coordinate with support for customer-facing message.
tess: do we have a quick hotpatch we can apply? prefer feature-flag flip over rollback.
adrian: yes. patch:
```bash
# disable prefetch for longctx models
curl -X POST "https://config-api.prod.internal/v1/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"flag":"continuous.prefetch","value":false,"scope":"canary-2026-05-17-12:40"}'
```
apply now?
maya: also run eviction flush for the prefetch keyspace to drop the noise:
```bash
# eviction helper - identifies keys with prefix longctx:yaRN:prefetch and touch to force eviction
python ops/tools/kv_flush.py --prefix longctx:yaRN:prefetch --dry-run
python ops/tools/kv_flush.py --prefix longctx:yaRN:prefetch --apply
```
eli: support: we need a short status line for customers (incidents page). Suggest: "We are investigating elevated errors for long-context requests; mitigations in progress. No data loss."
adrian: flipping flag now. Pushed to canary scope at 1945670000.
deploy-bot: config change applied: continuous.prefetch=false (scope=canary-2026-05-17-12:40) by adrian.
maya: within ~30s eviction rate dropped by 60% on the canary hosts, latency p95 improving. still seeing some carryover in dedicated pools.
kai: also lowering NTK lookahead to 128 as a secondary mitigation (less aggressive prefetch). I'll push that as a param change in model-profile for canary.
adrian: pushed: model-profile.ntk.lookahead=128 (canary). applied at 1945671500.
tess: rolling to prod? wanna confirm stability in canary for 30m before wider rollout.
maya: agree. but we should also guard: enable per-request prefetch throttling and increase kv cache eviction threshold temporarily to avoid oscillation.
adrian: added throttling rule: continuous.prefetch.rate_limit=50req/s per-model per-region (canary).
incident-bot: metric alert cleared for canary cluster at 1945673200; hosted-us-east-1 still elevated.
eli: customers A & B reported reduced errors after ~5m but some still see blips. created support ticket INC-5521 and notified CS.
kai: found reproduction locally: a concurrent stream of longctx requests with overlapping prefixes causes the prefetcher to hammer KV index and create garbage entries faster than eviction can reclaim. Sliding-window window-size=1024 is too aggressive for NTK with high token overlap.
adrian: long-term, we need better per-key rate limiting and smarter merge dedupe for prefetch. For now: schedule hotfix rollout to prod only after 40m stable canary.
tess: @oncall rotation: I'm handing off to maya for the next shift at 1945680000. leaving notes: watch kv_evictions, p95 latency, customer tickets.
maya: acknowledged handoff. I'll be primary for next 2 hours.
eli: posted customer-facing note on status.redwood.ai: "Mitigation applied; we are monitoring. Short-term impact may persist for high token-count calls."
adrian: after 36 minutes canary is stable. beginning staged rollout to prod with same flag flip and ntk lookahead change. rolling by region: us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 -> ap-south-1.
deploy-bot: staged rollout started at 1945679000, batchSize=30% nodes.
maya: during staged rollout we saw a small regression in eu-west-1 at 1945680500 — a node with older kv eviction tuning triggered a local spike. paused rollout and applied per-node eviction patch via autoscaler: set kv.eviction_target=0.7 on that node.
adrian: applied per-node patch and resumed.
incident-bot: all rollout batches completed at 1945682000. global kv_evictions back to baseline by 1945682200.
eli: support: customers updated; closing INC-5521 as mitigations resolved; pending postmortem.
tess: thanks everyone. follow-ups: - postmortem describing root cause (prefetch + sliding window + NTK overlap) - action items: per-key prefetch dedupe, prefetch circuit-breaker, safer defaults for lookahead, add chaos tests to catch kv-surge, telemetry to correlate prefetch rate -> eviction.
maya: opened PM-1243 and assigned owners. I'll lead postmortem.
kai: I'll prepare a benchmark comparing lookahead values and memory pressure.
adrian: will add runtime guardrails and a canary test that simulates longctx hammer.
tess: closing thread from on-call perspective. leaving final note: Incident severity: Sev3, customer impact limited/intermittent, root cause suspected interplay between YaRN sliding-window prefetch and NTK overlapping requests, mitigation=feature-flag flip + lookahead reduction + staged rollout. :white_check_mark:
